result:
No type errors. The build succeeds cleanly and type-checks pass.

Summary of what I implemented for Phase 3 (Transcribe / Speech), per SPEC.md §5:

- **`app/assets/sample.wav`** — copied the bundled audio file so Vite's static-copy plugin ships it inside the app bundle (confirmed at `nsbenchmark.app/app/assets/sample.wav`, matching `knownFolders.currentApp()`).
- **`App_Resources/iOS/Info.plist`** — added `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` (no microphone permission needed since transcription reads from a file, not live audio).
- **`app/components/Transcribe.vue`** — wired to `SFSpeechRecognizer`/`SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest` (raw Speech framework APIs via `@nativescript/types`, following the same completion-handler style as the existing `Health.vue`):
  - Status line reflects not-requested / granted / denied (denied covers both `Denied` and `Restricted`), refreshed on every navigation to the screen.
  - `Request Access` calls `SFSpeechRecognizer.requestAuthorization`.
  - `Transcribe Sample` is enabled only when granted and idle; starts a `shouldReportPartialResults` recognition task against the bundled file, streams partial results live into the transcript area, shows `Transcribing…` while running, and on the final result shows the transcript plus `Completed in N.N s` (wall-clock from tap to final result).
  - Errors from the recognizer or missing/unavailable recognizer surface in the status line and re-enable the button.

`ns build ios` succeeds and `vue-tsc --noEmit` reports no type errors.
